title: Slow-Roast Pork Belly
subtitle: Slow-cooked pork belly with crisp crackling
excerpt: A thick slab of pork belly slow-roasted for three hours until the meat is yielding and rich, then blasted at high heat to turn the skin into blistered, crackling. The most rewarding of all pork roasts.

recipe.sourceNotes: Slow-roast pork belly has become one of the most popular British roasts, rehabilitated from a cheap, fatty cut to a restaurant staple in the 2000s. The belly is the fattiest part of the pig, with layers of fat and meat running through it that baste the meat as it cooks, making it essentially self-basting and almost impossible to dry out. The crackling requires the opposite conditions from the slow-roasted meat beneath it: high heat and dry skin. The key technique is to score the skin deeply, dry it thoroughly, and season it with salt but not oil, then start the roast skin-side up for maximum crackling exposure.

recipeTools.notes: A deep roasting tin large enough to hold the belly flat.

content.text: The skin must be completely dry for crackling to form. Score it deeply in parallel lines 1 cm apart with a sharp knife or Stanley blade. Pat dry with kitchen paper. Salt generously and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight if time allows: this dries the skin further. Do not baste the skin during cooking. If the crackling has not blistered after the final blast, place the belly under a hot grill for 3 to 5 minutes.

items.preparation: halved, to rest the belly on

content.text: If time allows, salt the skin generously and leave uncovered in the fridge for several hours or overnight. On the day, heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Rub the flesh side with fennel seeds, black pepper, and garlic. Place the pork skin-side up on halved onions in a roasting tin. Pour the wine around (not over) the pork.
Roast for 3 hours until the meat is completely tender when pierced with a skewer. Remove from the oven.

Increase the oven to 240 C / fan 220 C / gas 9. Return the pork for 20 to 25 minutes until the skin is blistered and deeply golden. Watch carefully. Rest for 15 minutes. Cut between the score lines into thick slices. Serve with apple sauce and roasted vegetables.
